observation_summary: The BrentSolver.solve method returns the function value (yMin or yMax) instead of the root (min or max) when one of the endpoints is the root.
hypothesis: The solver implementation incorrectly returns the evaluated function value at the endpoints instead of the endpoint coordinates themselves when a root is detected at the boundary.
prediction: The code will contain a return statement that returns f.value(min) or f.value(max) instead of returning min or max directly when the root check passes.
experiment_rationale: The bug report explicitly states that the solver returns yMin/yMax instead of min/max. This indicates a procedural error in the solver's return logic when a root is identified at an endpoint.
reasoning_summary: The issue is a procedural error in the solver's logic where it returns the wrong value (the function evaluation result instead of the input coordinate). This is a classic algorithmic/method-level error in the implementation of the solver's return path, not a missing guard or a simple initialization error.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not an incorrect constant or variable initialization, but a procedural error in the return logic of the solver algorithm.
While the solver checks for roots, the failure is in the return value, not in the logic of the check itself.
